text: Next.js · Express.js · Supabase PostgreSQL · JWT RBAC
The project satisfies the core mini CRM requirements and keeps the original full stack template structure.
Lead capture, listing, search, filters, sorting, details, notes and status updates
Dashboard metrics from PostgreSQL aggregation functions
JWT login, admin and CRM roles, User Master for admin users
Next.js frontend, Express API, Supabase PostgreSQL and layered backend code
The implementation keeps the existing separation between UI, API proxy, backend layers and database routines.
Browser calls same-origin /api routes so the HttpOnly auth cookie stays protected
Express receives Bearer tokens from the proxy and enforces role access
Repositories call stored PostgreSQL functions through a shared pool
Each request moves through a small number of predictable layers.
Define REST paths and attach auth or role middleware.
Read req params/body and return the standard API response.
Validate input, check permissions, and decide 400/404 behavior.
Call parameterized PostgreSQL functions. SQL stays out of controllers.
The schema stores CRM data with constraints, indexes and database functions.
Stores contact details, budget, location, property type, source, status and timestamps.
Stores comments for a lead. Foreign key cascade removes notes when a lead is deleted.
Stores login accounts and role assignment for admin and CRM users.
Return API-ready JSON from PostgreSQL for CRUD, notes, dashboard and users.
The backend now exposes REST-style endpoints while preserving compatibility aliases.
Leads: POST, GET, GET by ID, PUT, DELETE
Dashboard: GET /api/dashboard with COUNT and GROUP BY aggregation
Users: admin-only list, view, create, edit and delete
The UI uses App Router pages and small client components for interactive workflows.
Responsive sidebar, top search and role-aware navigation.
Live metrics, status distribution and recent lead view.
Search, status tabs, source dropdown, sort controls and row actions.
Admin workspace to create, view, edit and delete users.
The app protects authenticated workflows and rejects invalid input before database writes.
JWT includes user ID, role and expiry, then moves through the Next proxy as a Bearer token
HttpOnly cookies prevent browser JavaScript from reading the token
Lead entity validates required fields, optional email format, allowed status and nonnegative budget
Admin-only routes protect User Master and lead deletion
The backend and frontend deploy as separate services with explicit environment configuration.
Root directory backend, build command npm ci, start command npm start.
Root directory frontend, build command npm run build.
API_BASE_URL points Next.js to the Render backend. Secrets stay out of Git.
Run db:setup or execute schema.sql and functions.sql in Supabase.
These upgrades would make PropLead feel closer to a production CRM.
Lead assignment with owner, priority and SLA due date
Kanban pipeline for New, Contacted, Site Visit and Closed stages
Follow-up reminders with email or WhatsApp notification hooks
Audit log for status, owner and user-management changes
CSV import/export, duplicate detection and bulk actions
Forecasting dashboard with source quality, closure time and budget pipeline
Both scaling styles can work together. The right choice depends on traffic, database load and operational cost.
Increase CPU, RAM and database capacity. Use a larger Render instance and Supabase compute plan when traffic grows gradually.
Run multiple stateless API instances behind a load balancer. Keep JWT auth and database state outside the server.
Use Supabase pooler, indexes, read replicas for reporting and query pagination to reduce pressure on the primary database.
Let Vercel serve static assets globally and keep API proxy routes lightweight.
A safe upgrade plan avoids large rewrites and keeps the current assignment features stable.
Add audit_log, lead_owner and follow_up_due_at columns with migrations
Create service methods and PostgreSQL functions for assignment, reminders and activity history
Add Kanban and calendar views using the existing lead API response shape
Move heavy analytics into read-only dashboard functions or materialized views
Introduce tests for auth, permissions, lead workflows and user management before scaling changes
The project demonstrates full stack ownership across UI, API design, data modeling and deployment.
I reused the template architecture instead of replacing it
I kept validation in the entity and service layer so controllers stay simple
I used PostgreSQL constraints and functions to protect data integrity
I added role-based workflows and kept browser auth in an HttpOnly cookie
I can explain how the app scales vertically first and horizontally when the API becomes stateless
